subject: Capacity validation report — OpticPay onboarding plan
messages:
From: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
To: jane.foster@opticpay.com
Cc: monica.patel@redwood.ai, connor.obrien@redwood.ai, dev.patel@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 01 Jul 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Capacity validation & test plan for OpticPay onboarding

Hi Jane —

Thanks again for the sync yesterday. Per our onboarding checklist, we want to run a focused capacity validation so we can sign off on the performance acceptance criteria before we move you to Dedicated capacity. Below is the test plan we intend to run from Redwood's US region. Please confirm the test window and whether you can provide a small representative dataset and a service account to use for telemetry.

Planned tests (high-level):
- Warm-start load: ramp 0 -> 50 concurrent streams over 10 minutes, sustained 30 min. Target: p95 <= 220 ms (inference only), median token throughput >= 1200 tokens/sec aggregate.
- Cold-start stress: 5 cold node restarts during a 60-minute window to validate KV cache warmup behavior; measure recovery latency and overall error rate <= 0.5%.
- Burst/steady-state mix: interleave short bursts (100 concurrent qps for 2 minutes) with steady 20-concurrency background. Verify no tail-latency spikes > 500ms.
- End-to-end sample load: gated test using a 1k sample of opt-in production-like messages to verify model quality and latency under load.

Attachments: opticpay_onboarding-plan.xlsx (test matrix and scripts), test-scripts.tar.gz (load generator + driver configs).

Acceptance / pass criteria (preliminary):
1) P95 inference latency under target in the warm-start test.
2) Successful KV cache recovery after node restarts with <2x warm penalty and acceptable error rates.
3) No more than 1% throttling/errors attributable to Redwood routing.
4) No model-quality regressions on the sample prompt set (we'll run the small eval suite and share diffs).

Proposed test window: Jul 8, 09:00 - 12:00 PT (we can also do Jul 9 if that works better).

Next steps:
- Please confirm test window and provide the sample dataset or a placeholder dataset by EOD Jul 6.
- Confirm which tokens/IDs we should use for telemetry and which endpoints you want exercised (chat/generation/embeddings).

I'll coordinate with our infra team (Connor/Dev) to run the scripts and capture Grafana + raw CSV exports.

Thanks,
Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Manager, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Capacity validation results and next steps — OpticPay (Jul 9 run)

Hi all — attaching the run artifacts and a short summary of the Jul 9 run. Quick TL;DR: we hit the acceptance criteria for the warm-start and burst tests; cold restart recovery showed a measurable warm penalty (expected) but within our defined tolerance after a short memo. Full data attached.

Summary highlights:
- Warm-start (50 concurrent streams, 30 min sustained): p50=95ms, p95=210ms, p99=310ms (note p99 tail corresponds to a single node restart event at 00:18 in the run).
- Token throughput aggregate: median ~1,320 tokens/sec across the pool; peak bursts recorded 1,850 tokens/sec for 2-minute windows.
- Cold-start restarts: average cold penalty 1.8x on p95 for the first 60 tokens; after 500 tokens penalty drops to ~1.15x. Error rate observed 0.37% (within target).
- Tail-latency during bursts: isolated spikes to ~620ms correlated with network oversubscription on one host; mitigation item below.

Pass/Fail: PASS (with operational notes).

Operational notes / follow-ups:
1) KV cache warmup: to reduce first-60-token penalty, we recommend a short pre-warm routine executed at client startup or a lightweight synthetic prefix heat. We'll include a script in the drive folder.
2) Host oversubscription: one host hit CPU contention during the largest burst; we've scheduled a soft cap on per-host concurrency for your Dedicated pool and a one-time rebalancing job.
3) Quality check: no significant model-quality regressions on the sample eval; diffs attached as csv. Please review.

Attachments included: capacity-validation-results-20260710.csv (CSV, 420KB); grafana-snapshots-20260710.zip (zip, 24MB). All raw traces uploaded to Drive.

Next steps:
- Redwood: we'll open a JIRA ticket for the rebalancing and attach the remediation plan (SUP-4121).
- OpticPay: review the diffs and confirm whether to proceed to Dedicated provisioning; if yes, we'll prepare a capacity reservation quote and expected SLA start date.

Let us know if you'd like a follow-up call next week to walk through the dashboards.

Thanks,
Connor O'Brien
Infra Lead — Redwood Inference
connor.obrien@redwood.ai
